newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business - July 25.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- SHELL AIMS FOR 50 PER CENT OF INTERGEN

Royal Dutch Shell has expressed an interest in acquiring a 50 per cent stake in the International Generating Company power generating subsidiary of US engineering and construction group Bechtel. Shell's Shell International Gas arm is seeking to complete negotiations with Bechtel by the end of September and would not comment on the likely cost of the acquisition. International Generating currently holds over 20 generating, pipeline, fuel and gasline operations.
-- VIDEOLOGIC LEADS RACE TO SUPPLY SEGA'S NEW CHIPS

British multimedia chip designer Videologic is reported to be close to signing a lucrative deal with Sega to supply its technology to Sega's next generation of video games machines. Videologic would not comment on its prospects, but its chances seem heightened following Sega's announcement on Wednesday that it would not be using chips made by Videologic's rival, 3DFX.
-- VIRTUALITY DEAL WINS US BACKING

UK virtual reality technology group Virtuality has sold its consumer headsets business to Retinal Displays of the US for an undisclosed sum. Virtuality's entertainment division's assets were sold in June and the group's administrators, are hoping to sell its professional headsets division and assets in the US before the end of the year. The UK group will retain its core development team and has acquired the support of licensing partners Takara and Philips.
THE TIMES
-- ARNAULT DIGS IN ON DRINKS MERGER

Bernard Arnault, the head of luxury foods group LVMH has stated he would prefer to obstruct the planned merger with Guinness and Grand Metropolitan, rather than compromise his proposals, which he labelled 'not negotiable'. Arnault, in London on Thursday looking to amass institutional shareholder support for his stance, stated it would not make sense to give up control of Moet Hennessy 'and get an uncontrolled stake in an unquoted company'.
-- KINGFISHER SET TO SWOOP ON FRENCH TAKEOVER TARGET

Retail conglomerate Kingfisher is examining the possibility of acquiring the remaining 74 per cent of French furniture and electrical retailer BUT for an estimated 225m stg. Kingfisher, which also owns Comet, Woolworths and B&Q, was forced to issue a statement declaring it would pay 'a price not exceeding FFr300 per share' following a sharp rise in BUT stocks Thursday, but added no further comment on a deal would be made until September.
-- BOOTS PRICE TAKES STEP BACKWARDS

Retailer Boots released its first quarter results on Thursday, indicating sales for its Boots Healthcare International over-the-counter medicine manufacturing arm were up 5.9 per cent like-for-like and 13 per cent overall, and sales at DIY chain Do-It-All were up only 2.4 per cent. Halford's same stores sales were up 3.4 per cent, Boots Opticians sales rose 24.1 per cent and Boots The Chemists sales increased 5.1 per cent. The less-than- impressive sales caused shares in the group to tumble 29p to 787p.
THE GUARDIAN
-- HARPERCOLLINS TO COME OFF REMAINDERED SHELF

Rupert Murdoch is reportedly close to reaching a sale of News Corporation's HarperCollins publishing arm, with German media group Bertelsmann tipped as a likely buyer for the business. Murdoch has been under a great deal of pressure of late to sell unprofitable areas of News Corp, due to the purchase of the LA Dodgers baseball team, cable network Family Entertainment, and direct marketer Heritage Media and sources close to the media tycoon claim he has 'washed his hands' of HarperCollins.
-- RAILTRACK VOWS TO SPEED UP CRASH COMPENSATION

Sir Robert Horton, chairman of UK rail group Railtrack, has pledged to quicken the pace of moves to settle compensation claims for railway accident victims. The pledge follows pressure from shareholders and MP David Kidney at a Railtrack meeting in London on Thursday, accompanied by claims by Rail, Maritime and Transport Union leader Jimmy Knapp that fragmentation in the rail industry gave individual companies the opportunity to avoid their responsibilities to victims.
-- COOKSON RESHUFFLE MAY COST 2M STG

Don Carcieri, the joint managing director of flower pots to computer parts group Cookson, is to depart the company with a 2m stg pay-off as a result of a recent reshuffle of boardroom employees. Cookson chairman Robert Malpas will retire, with current chief executive Richard Oster taking his place, while Carceri's fellow joint managing director, Steve Howard, will become chief executive. Cookson, meanwhile, has reported better-than-expected first half profits up from 69.2m stg to 85.4m stg.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CHANNEL 5 AND ITV BATTLE FOR DISNEY FILMS

Lord Hollick could be facing a conflict of interest, as Channel 5 and ITV, the two UK television channels in which he is a shareholder, are locked in a bidding war for the rights to films produced by Disney. A United spokesperson declared the decision would not be up to Hollick, however, and ITV stated its strong board would 'remove any possibility' of such a conflict. No price has been given for the 80-100 Disney films, though Channel 5 in May paid $140m for 60 Warner Bros releases and has a $10m contract with Columbia Tri-Star and a $40-$60m deal with Fox.
-- SETON POISED FOR 40M STG EXPANSION IN EUROPE

Medical products group Seton Healthcare is set to make its first non-UK acquisition in a deal which has been estimated at up to 40m stg. Seton is rumoured to be negotiating with five private healthcare companies in Europe, with its preferred markets identified as Holland, Germany and Scandinavia. If Seton is successful in its acquisitions, analysts suggest it would give the company enough infrastructure to build a significant non-UK business, with control over marketing and prices.
-- CLEAN SWEEP AT TROCADERO

The Trocadero leisure group has appointed John Conlan as its chairman and Nick Tamblyn as managing director, and given the two shares and options as part of an incentive plan intended to give them between six and seven per cent of the group after three years. The appointments come in wake of the sale of Trocadero and London Pavilion to Nigel Wray's Buford property group for a deal estimated at up to 210m stg. Conlan said Trocadero holds 'tremendous potential', noting he would use its 73m stg net cash to develop the group in outside retail leisure.
